rubriker.title: US Championships: So and Liang remain perfect, Paragua beats Yip
rubriker._rss_content: Wesley So and Awonder Liang remain the only players with perfect scores in the open section of the US Championship after two rounds. Fabiano Caruana stands alone in third place, half a point behind. In the women's tournament, the two lowest-rated participants, Thalia Cervantes and 13-year-old Megan Paragua, share the lead on 2/2. Paragua defeated defending champion Carissa Yip, who blundered in an equal position. | Photo: Lennart Ootes / Saint Louis Chess Club

rubriker.title: U.S. Championship: Round 1
rubriker._rss_content: Round 1 in Saint Louis on October 9 left three players at 1/1 in the open section, with Wesley So, Awonder Liang and Jeffery Xiong all winning with White, and Fabiano Caruana opening with a 17-move draw. The women’s section was even more decisive, as four wins produced a four-way tie at the top while defending champion Carissa Yip started with a draw.

rubriker.title: Hikaru Nakamura Wins Bullet Brawl Oct 10 2026
The strange comforts of superstition in chess
rubriker._rss_content: Chess sells itself as a contest of calculation, where chance has been removed. Yet some elite players keep lucky pens, repeat outfits and meals, or give a cat a place in their pre-game routine. The interesting question is not whether a lucky charm can change a position on the board; it is why people reach for one when the result matters and control feels limited. | Pictured: Alexander Alekhine and his cat Chess (Amsterdam, 1935)

rubriker.title: Between the Silk Road and the chessboard - eight days in Uzbekistan
rubriker._rss_content: Besides the spectacular Chess Olympiad, Uzbekistan and the city of Samarkand had much more to offer, including friendly people and 2,500 years of culture. Axel Eger attended the Olympiad and took the opportunity to explore the country and get to know its people. Here is his travel report. | Photos: Axel Eger

rubriker.title: Israeli Players Barred from Amateur Chess Championships inMalaysia
rubriker._rss_content: Wadim Rosenstein has criticised FIDE over the potential exclusion of Israeli players from the upcoming World Amateur Chess Championship in Malaysia, questioning whether the international federation applies its own rules consistently.

rubriker.title: Anish Giri Joins Women's Chess Team After Controversial 4NCL Gender Rule
rubriker._rss_content: Dutch grandmaster Anish Giri has made his debut for She Plays To Win Lionesses A in the British Four Nations Chess League (4NCL), following a controversy over rules requiring the previously all-female team to recruit a male player.

rubriker.title: Turlov's €30 Million Plan for FIDE: What It Funds and What It Leaves Unsaid
rubriker._rss_content: FIDE president Timur Turlov is promising to put about €30 million into chess over four years, according to a report in the Cyprus Mail, with a spending plan covering development grants, federation media support, a digital platform for players and a push into artificial intelligence.
